paragraphs: Verizon Communications Inc. (the Company) is a holding company that, acting through its subsidiaries (together with the Company, collectively, Verizon), is one of the world's leading providers of communications, technology, information and streaming products and services to consumers, businesses and government entities. With a presence around the world, we offer data, video and voice services and solutions on our networks and platforms that are designed to meet customers' demand for mobility, reliable network connectivity and security.
We have two reportable segments that we operate and manage as strategic business units - Verizon Consumer Group (Consumer) and Verizon Business Group (Business).

Our Consumer segment provides consumer-focused wireless and wireline communications services and products. Our wireless services are provided across one of the most extensive wireless networks in the United States (U.S.) under the Verizon family of brands and through wholesale and other arrangements. As of the date this report is being filed, our wireline services are provided in 31 U.S. states and Washington D.C. over our 100% fiber-optic network through our fiber product portfolio, as well as over a traditional copper-based network. We also provide fixed wireless access (FWA) broadband through our fifth-generation (5G) or fourth-generation (4G) Long-Term Evolution (LTE) networks as an alternative to traditional landline internet access.

In 2025, the Consumer segment's revenues were $106.8 billion, representing approximately 77% of Verizon's consolidated revenues. As of December 31, 2025, Consumer had approximately 116 million wireless retail connections (including FWA), of which 83% were postpaid connections. In addition, at December 31, 2025, Consumer had approximately 11 million total broadband connections (which includes Fios internet, FWA and Digital Subscriber Line (DSL) connections), and approximately 2 million Fios video connections.

Our Business segment provides wireless and wireline communications services and products, including mobility communication services, FWA and wireline broadband, Internet of Things (IoT) connectivity solutions, advanced communication services, corporate networking solutions, local and long distance voice services, and security and managed network services. We provide these products and services to businesses, public sector customers and wireless and wireline carriers across the U.S. and a subset of these products and services to customers around the world.

In 2025, the Business segment's revenues were $29.1 billion, representing approximately 21% of Verizon's consolidated revenues. As of December 31, 2025, Business had approximately 31 million wireless retail postpaid connections (including FWA) and approximately 3 million total broadband connections (which includes Fios internet, FWA and DSL connections).

Additional discussion of our reportable segments is included in Item 7 under the headings "Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations — Overview" and "— Segment Results of Operations" and in Note 13 to the consolidated financial statements included in this Annual Report.
We provide a wide variety of wireless services to Consumer and Business customers on different service plan options.

Our Consumer Group offers various phone plans for retail customers with features, designed to fit their needs, including access to their preferred content and services (which we call "perks"). We also offer plans for customers who want access to Verizon's network at a lower price point, as well as discounts and special rate plans for qualifying customers. Our Business customers can choose from a variety of plans with different features to meet their specific needs.

Customers can obtain our wireless services on a postpaid or prepaid basis. Retail (non-wholesale) postpaid accounts primarily represent retail customers that are directly served and managed by Verizon and use Verizon branded services. A single account may include monthly wireless services for a variety of connected devices. Our postpaid service is generally billed one month in advance for a monthly access charge in return for access to and usage of network services. Our prepaid service is offered only to Consumer customers and enables individuals to obtain wireless services without credit verification by paying for all services in advance. As of December 31, 2025, we had 96 million postpaid connections and 20 million prepaid connections, representing approximately 83% and 17% of our Consumer wireless retail connections, respectively.

We also provide FWA broadband through our 5G or 4G LTE wireless networks to our Consumer and Business customers. FWA enables fixed broadband access using radio frequencies instead of cables and can be used to connect homes and businesses to the internet. As of December 31, 2025, we had 5.7 million FWA broadband connections.

Consumer and Business offer several categories of wireless equipment to customers, including a variety of smartphones and other handsets, wireless-enabled internet devices, such as tablets, and other wireless-enabled connected devices, such as smart watches. Oftentimes, we offer promotional trade-in offers to incentivize new customers or existing customer upgrades. Consumer wireless customers can acquire wireless equipment from us using device payment plans, which permit the customer to pay for the device in installments over time.

In addition to wireless services and equipment for retail customers, the Consumer segment sells residential fixed connectivity solutions, including internet, video and voice services, and wireless network access to resellers on a wholesale basis. Consumer also provides non-connectivity services including device protection, content offerings, cloud storage, and other products.

Residential fixed services – We provide residential fixed connectivity solutions to customers over our 100% fiber-optic network through our fiber product portfolio and over a traditional copper-based network. We also provide FWA broadband through both 5G and 4G LTE home internet offerings, which are available in most states across the U.S.

headings: We face significant competition that may negatively affect our operating results.

Adverse conditions in the U.S. and international economies, changes to international trade and tariff policies and related economic and geopolitical factors could impact our results of operations and financial condition.
Cyberattacks impacting our networks or systems could have an adverse effect on our business.
Our long-term success depends on our ability to implement business transformation initiatives and achieve their anticipated benefits.
System failures and disruptions to our networks and operations could prevent us from providing reliable service to customers and adversely affect our business.
We depend on key suppliers and vendors to provide services and equipment that we need to operate our business.
A significant portion of our workforce is represented by labor unions, and we could incur additional costs or experience work stoppages as a result of the renegotiation of our labor contracts.
Damage to our reputation or brands could adversely affect our business.
Changes in the regulatory framework under which we operate could adversely affect our business prospects or results of operations.
Our business may be impacted by changes in tax laws and regulations, or their interpretations, and challenges to our tax positions.
We are subject to a substantial amount of litigation, which could require us to pay significant damages or settlements.
Verizon has a significant amount of debt, which could increase further if we incur additional debt in the future and do not retire existing debt.
Adverse changes in the financial markets and other factors could increase our borrowing costs and reduce the availability of financing.
Increases in costs for pension benefits and active and retiree healthcare benefits may reduce our profitability and increase our funding commitments.
There can be no assurance that our current or future share repurchase programs will be fully consummated or that we will continue to increase our dividend.
We are subject to risks associated with mergers, acquisitions, divestitures and other strategic transactions.
paragraphs: The following discussion of "Risk Factors" identifies factors that may adversely affect our business, operations, financial condition or future performance. This information should be read in conjunction with "Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Result of Operations" and the consolidated financial statements and related notes. The following discussion of risks is not all-inclusive but is designed to highlight what we believe are the material factors to consider when evaluating our business and expectations. These factors could cause our future results to differ materially from our historical results and from expectations reflected in forward-looking statements.

We face significant competition in our industries. The rapid development of new technologies, services and products has eliminated many of the traditional distinctions among wireless, cable, internet and other communication services and brought new competitors to our markets, including other telecommunications companies, cable companies, wireless service providers, satellite providers, and others. While these changes have enabled us to offer new types of products and services, they have also allowed other providers to broaden the scope of their own competitive offerings. If we are unable to successfully differentiate our services and products from our competitors, it could adversely affect our competitive position and market share.

Our competitors commonly offer aggressive pricing, promotions, premium content options and other incentives – in some cases specifically targeting our customers and putting pressure on our pricing and margins. In addition, we expect the wireless industry's customer growth rate to continue to moderate over time in comparison to historical growth rates, leading to increased competition for customers. Our ability to compete effectively will depend on, among other things, the pricing of our products and services and our value proposition, our competitors' promotional strategies, the quality of our customer service, our network

reliability, speed, capacity and coverage, our ability to market our products and services effectively, our development of new and enhanced products and services, our capital resources, and the reach and quality of our sales and distribution channels. It will also depend on how successfully we anticipate and respond to various factors affecting our industries, including changes in consumer preferences and demand for existing services, new technologies and business models, such as the increasing use of AI and machine learning technologies, demographic and immigration trends, evolving geopolitical and economic conditions, including inflation, and regulatory changes. If we are not able to respond successfully to these competitive challenges, our results of operations and financial condition could be adversely impacted. In addition, a sustained decline in a reporting unit's revenues and earnings has resulted in the past, and may again result in the future, in a significant negative impact on its fair value requiring us to record an impairment charge, which could have an adverse impact on our results of operations.

If we are not able to take advantage of developments in technology and address changing consumer demand on a timely basis, we may experience a decline in the demand for our services, be unable to implement our business strategy and experience reduced profits.

Our industries are rapidly changing as new technologies are developed that offer consumers an array of choices for their communications needs and allow new entrants into the markets we serve. In order to grow and remain competitive, we will need to adapt to future changes in technology, enhance our existing offerings and introduce new offerings to address our customers' changing demands and differentiate our services and products from our competitors. If we are unable to meet future challenges from competing technologies on a timely basis or at an acceptable cost, we could lose customers to our competitors. We may not be able to accurately predict technological trends or the success of new services in the market. If our new services fail to gain acceptance in the marketplace, or if costs associated with the implementation and introduction of these services materially increase, our ability to retain and attract customers could be adversely affected.

With a presence around the world, we offer data, video and voice services and solutions on our networks and platforms that are designed to meet customers' demand for mobility, reliable network connectivity and security. To compete effectively in today's dynamic marketplace, we are focused on delivering what customers want and need in the digital world by offering innovative products and services, delivering excellent customer experience, and leveraging the capabilities of our high-performing networks.
We have two reportable segments that we operate and manage as strategic business units - Consumer and Business.

Our Consumer segment provides consumer-focused wireless and wireline communications services and products. Our wireless services are provided across one of the most extensive wireless networks in the U.S. under the Verizon family of brands and through wholesale and other arrangements. As of the date this report is being filed, our wireline services are provided in 31 U.S. states and Washington D.C. over our 100% fiber-optic network through our fiber product portfolio, as well as over a traditional copper-based network. We also provide FWA broadband through our 5G or 4G LTE networks as an alternative to traditional landline internet access.

Customers can obtain our wireless services on a postpaid or prepaid basis. Our postpaid service is generally billed one month in advance for a monthly access charge in return for access to and usage of network services. Our prepaid service is offered only to Consumer customers and enables individuals to obtain wireless services without credit verification by paying for all services in advance. The Consumer segment also offers several categories of wireless equipment to customers, including a variety of smartphones and other handsets, wireless-enabled internet devices, such as tablets, and other wireless-enabled connected devices, such as smart watches.

In addition to wireless services and equipment for retail customers, the Consumer segment sells residential fixed connectivity solutions, including internet, video and voice services, and wireless network access to resellers on a wholesale basis.

The Consumer segment's operating revenues for the year ended December 31, 2025 totaled $106.8 billion, an increase of $3.9 billion, or 3.8%, compared to the year ended December 31, 2024. See "Segment Results of Operations" for additional information regarding our Consumer segment's operating performance and selected operating statistics.

Our Business segment provides wireless and wireline communications services and products, including mobility communication services, FWA and wireline broadband, IoT connectivity solutions, advanced communication services, corporate networking solutions, local and long distance voice services, and security and managed network services. We provide these products and services to businesses, public sector customers and wireless and wireline carriers across the U.S. and a subset of these products and services to customers around the world.

The Business segment's operating revenues for the year ended December 31, 2025 totaled $29.1 billion, a decrease of $462 million, or 1.6%, compared to the year ended December 31, 2024. See "Segment Results of Operations" for additional information regarding our Business segment's operating performance and selected operating statistics.

Corporate and other primarily includes device insurance programs, investments in unconsolidated businesses and development stage businesses that support our strategic initiatives, as well as unallocated corporate expenses, certain pension and other employee benefit related costs and interest and financing expenses. Corporate and other also includes the historical results of divested businesses and other adjustments and gains and losses that are not allocated or used in assessing segment performance due to their nature. Although such transactions are excluded from the business segment results, they are included in reported consolidated earnings. Gains and losses from these transactions that are not individually significant are included in

segment results and therefore are included in the chief operating decision maker's assessment of segment performance. See "Consolidated Results of Operations" for additional information regarding Corporate and other results.

Our strategy requires significant capital investments primarily to acquire wireless spectrum, put the spectrum into service, provide additional capacity for growth in our networks, invest in fiber, evolve and maintain our networks and develop and maintain significant advanced information technology systems and data system capabilities. During the year ended December 31, 2025, these investments included $17.0 billion for capital expenditures. See "Cash Flows Used in Investing Activities" and "Liquidity and Capital Resources" for additional information.

We design, build and operate networks to provide connectivity and related services meeting the needs of our diverse customers: consumers, businesses, government organizations, first responders, and educational institutions.

We have a portfolio of spectrum holdings, including C-Band and millimeter wave spectrum, and are constantly transforming our networks by leveraging innovation and new technologies to deliver improved network performance and efficiency. Our networks leverage advanced technologies, including 5G wireless, fiber-based transport, cloud infrastructures, AI and automation, private networks and IP routing solutions. We are using the benefits of cloud computing and storage to virtualize aspects of our network infrastructure. We are densifying our networks by utilizing macro and small cell technology, in-building solutions and distributed antenna systems to increase coverage, improve quality of service and add capacity to accommodate an increasing number of users.

On January 20, 2026, we completed the acquisition of Frontier, a U.S. provider of broadband internet and other communication services. This transaction expanded our fiber broadband footprint to 31 U.S. states and Washington D.C., and provides opportunities for future growth.

paragraphs: Verizon Communications Inc. (the Company) 為一間控股公司，透過其子公司（與本公司合稱 Verizon）提供全球領先的通訊、科技、資訊及串流產品與服務，服務對象包括消費者、企業與政府機構。本公司在全球多處設有據點，提供資料、視訊與語音服務與解決方案，透過網路與平台設計以符合客戶對行動性、可靠網路連線與安全性之需求。
本公司有兩個應報告分部，作為戰略業務單位進行運作與管理 - Verizon Consumer Group (Consumer) 與 Verizon Business Group (Business)。

Consumer 分部提供以消費者為導向的無線與有線通訊服務與產品。本公司無線服務透過美國最廣泛的無線網路（U.S.）提供，品牌為 Verizon 家族品牌，並透過委外與其他安排提供服務。截至本報告提交之日，本公司有線服務於美國 31 個州與華盛頓特區透過本公司 100% 光纖網路，透過光纖產品組合提供服務，亦透過傳統銅線網路提供服務。本公司亦透過第五代（5G）或第四代（4G）長期演進（LTE）網路提供固定無線存取（FWA）寬頻服務，作為傳統陸線寬頻存取之替代方案。

2025 年，消費者應報告分部的營業收入為 106.8 十億美元，佔 Verizon 合併營業收入約 77%。截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，消費者應報告分部擁有約 116 百萬無線零售連線（包含 FWA），其中 83% 為後付費連線。此外，截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，消費者應報告分部擁有約 11 百萬總寬頻連線（包含 Fios 網際網路、FWA 及數位用戶線 (DSL) 連線），以及約 2 百萬 Fios 視訊連線。
Business 分部提供無線與有線通訊服務與產品，包括行動通訊服務、FWA 與有線寬頻、物聯網 (IoT) 連線解決方案、先進通訊服務、企業網路解決方案、本地與長途語音服務，以及安全與管理網路服務。本公司為美國境內企業、公部門客戶與無線與有線電信業者提供這些產品與服務，並為部分客戶提供這些產品與服務至全球。
關於本公司應報告分部之更多討論，請參閱本年度報告第 7 項「管理層對財務狀況與營運成果之分析與討論 — 總覽」與「— 分部營運成果」，以及本年度財務報表附註第 13 項。
本公司為 Consumer 與 Business 客戶提供多樣化的無線服務，並提供不同服務方案。
本公司消費者部門提供多種行動上網方案，供零售客戶使用，並具備符合其需求的特色功能，包括可存取其偏好的內容與服務（我們稱之為 "perks"）。本公司亦提供方案，供希望以較低價格使用 Verizon 網路的客戶，以及符合資格的客戶可享折扣與特殊費率方案。本公司企業客戶可選擇多種具不同功能的方案，以符合其特定需求。

客戶可依後付或預付方式取得本公司之無線服務。零售（非轉售）後付帳戶主要代表由 Verizon 直接服務與管理的零售客戶，並使用 Verizon 品牌服務。單一帳戶可能包含多種連接裝置的月度無線服務。本公司後付服務通常會預先收取一個月的費用，以換取使用網路服務的使用權。本公司預付服務僅提供給消費者客戶，使個人可在不進行信用審核的情況下取得無線服務，並預先支付所有服務費用。截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，本公司擁有 9600 萬個後付連線，以及 2000 萬個預付連線，分別約佔本公司消費者無線零售連線的 83% 與 17%。
本公司亦透過 5G 或 4G LTE 無線網路，為消費者與企業客戶提供 FWA 寬頻服務。FWA 可透過無線電頻率取代電纜，提供固定寬頻存取，可用於連接家庭與企業至互聯網。截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，本公司擁有 570 萬個 FWA 寬頻連線。
消費者與企業部門提供多種無線設備給客戶，包括多種智慧型手機與其他行動電話、具無線功能的網路裝置，例如平板電腦，以及其他具無線功能的連接裝置，例如智慧手錶。有時，本公司會提供促銷換購方案，以鼓勵新客戶或現有客戶升級。消費者無線客戶可透過本公司以裝置分期付款方案取得無線設備，使客戶可分期付款購買裝置。
除了零售客戶的無線服務與設備，消費者部門亦銷售住宅固定連接解決方案，包括網路、視訊與語音服務，以及以轉售方式向經銷商提供無線網路存取服務。消費者部門亦提供非連接服務，包括裝置保護、內容服務、雲端儲存及其他產品。
住宅固定服務 – 本公司透過 100% 光纖網路的光纖產品組合，為客戶提供住宅固定連接解決方案，並透過傳統電纜網路提供服務。本公司亦透過 5G 與 4G LTE 家用網路服務提供 FWA 寬頻服務，這些服務在美國大多數州皆可使用。

消費者分部於 2025 年 12 月 31 日為止的營業收入為 1068 億美元，較 2024 年 12 月 31 日為止的營業收入增加 39 億美元，或成長 3.8%。有關消費者分部營運表現與選定營運統計資料的更多資訊，請參閱「分部營運結果」。
企業分部提供無線與有線通訊服務與產品，包括行動通訊服務、FWA 及有線寬頻、物聯網連線解決方案、先進通訊服務、企業網路解決方案、本地與長途語音服務，以及安全與管理網路服務。本公司為美國的企業、公共部門客戶及無線與有線電信業者提供這些產品與服務，並為部分客戶提供這些產品與服務至全球各地。
企業及其它主要包含行動裝置保險方案、對未合併企業及發展階段企業的投資，以及未分配的企業費用、某些退休金及其他員工福利相關成本，以及利息及融資費用。企業及其它亦包含已出售業務的歷史結果及其他調整及獲利與損失，因其性質而未分配或未用於評估分部績效。雖然這些交易未包含在業務分部結果中，但已包含在報告的合併營收中。這些交易的獲利與損失，若個別不具重大性，則包含在
分部結果中，因此已包含在主要營運決策者評估分部績效的考量中。有關企業及其它結果的更多資訊，請參閱『合併營運成果』。
我們的策略需要大量的資本投資，主要用於取得無線電頻譜、將頻譜投入服務、為網路增長提供額外容量、投資光纖、演進及維護網路，以及發展及維護重要的先進資訊科技系統及資料系統能力。在截至2025年12月31日的會計年度中，這些投資包含170億美元的資本支出。有關更多資訊，請參閱『投資活動所使用的現金流』及『流動性及資本資源』。
我們設計、建造並營運網路，以提供符合我們多樣化客戶（包括消費者、企業、政府機構、第一 responders 及教育機構）需求的連線及相關服務。

我們擁有包含C-Band及毫米波頻譜的頻譜組合，並持續透過創新及新技術轉型網路，以提供改善的網路效能與效率。我們的網路運用先進技術，包括5G無線、光纖基礎的運輸、雲端基礎設施、AI及自動化、私有網路及IP路由解決方案。我們正利用雲端運算及儲存的優勢，將網路基礎設施虛擬化。我們透過運用宏觀及小型基地臺技術、室內解決方案及分散式天線系統來密集化網路，以增加覆蓋範圍、改善服務品質並增加容量，以因應日益增加的用戶數量。
2026年1月20日，我們完成對Frontier的收購，Frontier為美國的寬頻互聯網及其他通訊服務供應商。此交易將我們的光纖寬頻覆蓋範圍擴展至美國31個州及華盛頓特區，並為未來成長提供機會。

headings: 我們面臨激烈的競爭，可能對我們的營運成果產生負面影響。
美國與國際經濟環境惡化、國際貿易與關稅政策的變動，以及相關的總體經濟與地緣政治因素，可能影響我們的營運成果與財務狀況。
針對我們網路或系統的網路攻擊，可能對我們的業務產生負面影響。
我們的長期成功取決於我們能否落實業務轉型計畫並實現預期的效益。
系統故障及對我們網路與營運的中斷，可能導致我們無法為客戶提供穩定的服務，並對我們的業務產生負面影響。
我們依賴關鍵供應商與廠商提供我們營運所需的服務與設備。
本公司有相當多的員工屬於勞工工會所代表，因勞動契約重新談判，我們可能面臨額外成本或停工的情況。
本公司聲譽或品牌受損，可能對營運造成不利影響。
我們所處的法規架構若發生變更，可能對業務前景或營運結果造成不利影響。
本公司業務可能受稅法與稅務規範變更，或其解釋方式，以及對本公司稅務立場的挑戰所影響。
本公司面臨大量訴訟，可能需要支付重大賠償或和解金額。
威瑞森擁有相當多的債務，若未來增加債務而未能償還現有債務，債務可能進一步增加。
不利的金融市場變動及其他因素可能提高我們的借款成本並減少融資的可得性。
養老金福利及現任與退休員工醫療福利的成本增加，可能降低我們的利潤並增加我們的資金承諾。
無法保證我們目前或未來的股票回購計畫將完全執行，或我們將持續提高股息。
我們面臨與併購、資產買賣及其他戰略交易相關的風險。
paragraphs: 以下有關「風險因素」的討論識別出可能對本公司業務、營運、財務狀況或未來表現產生不利影響的因素。此資訊應與「管理層對財務狀況與營運結果之討論與分析」以及合併財務報表及其附註一併閱讀。以下有關風險的討論並非完整無遺，但係設計用以強調本公司認為在評估本公司業務與預期時應考慮的重要因素。這些因素可能導致本公司未來的結果與歷史結果以及反映在財務預測陳述中的預期有重大差異。

我們在產業中面臨著激烈的競爭。新技術、服務與產品的快速發展已消除許多傳統上無線、有線、網際網路及其他通訊服務之間的區別，並為我們的市場帶來新的競爭對手，包括其他電信業者、有線電視公司、無線服務提供者、衛星服務提供者等。雖然這些變化使我們能夠提供新類型的產品與服務，但也使其他服務提供者得以擴大其競爭產品的範圍。若我們無法成功地將我們的服務與產品與競爭對手區隔，可能會對我們的競爭地位與市佔率產生不利影響。
我們的競爭對手常提供激進的價格、促銷活動、高階內容選項及其他誘因－有時甚至針對我們的客戶，對我們的價格與毛利率造成壓力。此外，我們預期無線產業的客戶成長率將持續較歷史成長率為低，導致客戶競爭更加激烈。我們能否有效競爭，將取決於諸多因素，包括我們產品與服務的價格、我們的價值主張、競爭對手的促銷策略、我們的客戶服務品質以及我們的網路

可靠性、速度、容量及覆蓋範圍、我們有效市場我們產品與服務的能力、我們開發新產品與增強型產品與服務的能力、我們的資本資源、以及我們銷售與分銷渠道的觸及範圍與品質。這也會取決於我們預測並回應影響我們產業各項因素的成功程度，包括消費者偏好與現有服務需求的變化、新技術與商業模式，例如人工智能與機器學習技術的應用增加、人口統計與移民趨勢、不斷演變的國際政治與經濟條件，包括通貨膨脹，以及法規變更。若我們無法成功回應這些競爭挑戰，我們的營運結果與財務狀況可能會受到不利影響。此外，報表單位收入與獲利的持續下降，在過去曾導致顯著的負面影響於其公允價值，未來也可能再次導致此情況，使我們必須記錄減損費用，這可能會對我們的營運結果產生不利影響。
若我們無法善用科技發展並及時回應變動的消費者需求，我們可能會經歷服務需求下降、無法實施我們的業務策略並導致利潤減少。

我們的產業正在快速變遷，因為新技術的發展為消費者提供了多樣的通訊需求選擇，並允許新進企業進入我們服務的市場。為要成長並保持競爭力，我們需要適應未來的科技變動、增強現有產品與服務，並推出新產品與服務以回應消費者變動的需求，並與競爭對手的產品與服務區隔。若我們無法及時或以可接受的成本回應來自競爭科技的未來挑戰，我們可能會失去客戶給競爭對手。我們可能無法準確預測科技趨勢或新服務在市場上的成功程度。若我們的新服務未能在市場上獲得接受，或與這些服務的實施與推出相關的成本大幅增加，我們保留與吸引客戶的能力可能會受到不利影響。
